claims.text: A computational framework integrating machine learning and density functional theory can be used to design intrinsically strong, ductile, and low-weight RHEA compositions.
The framework can predict the properties of HEAs and RHEAs.
HEAs have a very large composition-selection space because they contain multiple principal elements.
Crystal structure and lattice parameters act as structural mediators for the predicted alloy properties.
Machine-learning algorithms can predict HEA and RHEA properties from composition and crystal structure.
Density functional theory provides accurate calculations of alloy electronic structure.
Density functional theory provides accurate calculations of alloy thermodynamic properties.
The designed RHEAs will exhibit a 20% strength increase relative to existing RHEA compositions.
The designed RHEAs will exhibit a 30% ductility increase relative to existing RHEA compositions.
The designed RHEAs will exhibit a 15% weight reduction relative to existing RHEA compositions.
The computational framework is limited to HEAs and RHEAs containing no more than five principal elements.
Framework accuracy may depend on training-data quality.
Framework accuracy may depend on the complexity of the machine-learning algorithms.
